chunks: And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, from Zakariyya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Regarding a person in ihram who hunted a bird in the Haram (sanctuary), struck it against the ground, and killed it, he said: 'Upon him are three valuations (kaffarah): one valuation for his ihram, one valuation for the Haram, and one valuation for his considering it small (deeming it insignificant).'

key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A pilgrim in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a bird while in ihram inside the Haram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting the cumulative nature of penalties in Shia jurisprudence where distinct violations incur separate compensations. The third valuation specifically addresses the psychological dimension of the sin—'istisghar' (considering the prey insignificant)—emphasizing that intent and perception of value are integral to the expiation. This tripartite structure underscores the sanctity of both the ritual state (ihram) and the physical space (Haram).
